terms.meaning: The ratio of a distance on a map to the real distance, in the same unit.
Two quantities that change by the same factor, so their quotient stays the same.
When one quantity is multiplied by n, the other is divided by n, so their product stays the same.
A circle cut into parts, where the angle of each part shows its share of the total.

items.name: Using a map scale
items.example: Scale 1 : 100000. 3 cm on the map is 300000 cm = 3 km.

items.name: Equal ratios with many terms
items.formula: Multiply every term by the same number

items.name: Dividing in the ratio p : q : r
items.formula: First part = p ÷ (p + q + r) × total

items.name: Angles of a triangle in a ratio
Rule for inverse proportion
items.example: 6 workers take 10 days. 12 workers take 6 × 10 ÷ 12 = 5 days.

items.name: Speed and time
items.formula: Speed × time = distance stays the same
items.example: At 5 km/h a trip takes 3 hours. At 15 km/h it takes 5 × 3 ÷ 15 = 1 hour.

items.name: Sharing the same total
items.formula: Number of parts × size of each part stays the same
items.example: 8 periods of 45 minutes is 360 minutes. With 9 periods, each is 360 ÷ 9 = 40 minutes.

mistakes.text: Check which kind of proportion it is. More workers means fewer days (inverse), but more items means more cost (direct).
Sides of a triangle cannot be in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5, because 1 + 3 is less than 5. Angles can.
A map ratio uses the same unit on both sides. For 1 : 100000, 1 cm means 100000 cm, not 100000 km.
In a pie chart the angles add up to 360°, not 100°.
